solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

definitions.meaning: a do is a party or celebration
to have a go at something is to have a ... at it

explanation.surface: A terse instruction: just do it, have a go.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British synonyms: a party is a bash, and an attempt is a bash.

indicators.note: to embrace means the first word's letters wrap around the second's

parts.note: gay in its older sense means happy or carefree
lax means relaxed or easy-going

explanation.surface: A cheerful, relaxed person throwing a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' reads as someone entertaining guests; here it is a multitude, as in a heavenly host of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great multitude, and a galaxy is a vast multitude of stars.

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaky, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: R is the chess notation for a rook, also called a castle

explanation.surface: Mysteries hidden in a castle built on a crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' is the anagram signal, not a description of the castle. R is the chess notation for the rook, also called a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist who created Horatio Hornblower was a British writer.

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A musician extemporising a break in a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks musical alongside 'improvised', but it is a split, RIFT, which is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To riff is to play short improvised phrases, especially on guitar.

clue.text: With casual chat, get on good TV show

indicators.note: casual means haphazard or random, so these letters are arranged loosely

parts.note: do means fare or get on, as in how are you doing

explanation.surface: Advice for a guest: chat informally and you'll get on a good programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casual' rearranges CHAT into ATCH. Watchdog is a long-running BBC consumer-affairs programme.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a British television programme investigating consumer complaints.

clue.text: Loud noise when low bass is turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
B is an abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A stereo's bass knob gets cranked and the room shakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suggests volume; here it reverses MOOB, a cow's low plus B, in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a deep, resonant loud sound.

clue.text: Handsome and very famous doom merchant

parts.note: handsome as in a handsome sum, a fat one
A-list describes the most famous celebrities

explanation.surface: A good-looking celebrity who is forever predicting disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes everything is predestined, often gloomily, is a merchant of doom in the humorous sense.

clue.text: Yank regularly found in wild frontier?

definitions.text: Yank regularly found in wild frontier?

indicators.note: found in means the picked letters are placed inside the other piece
wild means unruly, so the word frontier is rearranged
regularly means taking every other letter of the word Yank

explanation.surface: An American who habitually turns up in the untamed frontier lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges FRONTIER into FORTINER, and 'regularly' takes Y and N from Yank to sit within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1849 California gold rush drew American prospectors to the untamed western frontier.

clue.text: When to carry old lady's hoard

indicators.note: to carry means the first word's letters hold the second piece within them

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
one's old lady is one's mother, ma, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Mother's stash of savings, kept until needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoard is to accumulate and store up, which is to gather together.

parts.note: in a mo means in a moment, soon
to rat on someone is to betray them
love is zero in tennis scores, O

explanation.surface: A faithless partner who will soon betray the one they love.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian borrowing names a male lover or sweetheart.

definitions.meaning: to intercept and prevent something is to stop it
to set off in some direction is to go

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to intercept and forestall, and to set off somewhere.

clue.text: Little band possibly going on to play jazz?

indicators.note: going on to means the band's letters are placed after the other piece

parts.note: to comp in jazz is to play accompanying chords
a band is one kind of musical act

explanation.surface: A small group about to start a jazz set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little band' reads as a combo, but 'Little' is the definition and the band is an ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact means small and neatly packed, taking up little space.

clue.text: Setter hiding answer in the wrong way perhaps

indicators.note: hiding means the first piece conceals the others inside it

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

indicators.note: the wrong way means the little word is read backwards

parts.note: by can mean in, as in by night

explanation.surface: A crossword setter admitting he may have gone about something wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is not a container signal here: it stands for a synonym (as in by day), which 'the wrong way' reverses before 'hiding' tucks it and A inside the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express possibility without certainty; they are straightforward synonyms.

parts.note: ABS reads as an anti-lock braking system, but abs are abdominal muscles, so these are vehicles with brawn

explanation.surface: Cars equipped with anti-lock brakes.
explanation.walkthrough: ABS is the braking system; abs are stomach muscles, hence powerful American performance cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names powerful, high-performance American cars from the 1960s and 70s.

definitions.meaning: a sum taken off something is a subtraction
gathering means inferring or concluding, as in I gather

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a subtraction and an inference reached by reasoning.

clue.text: Device supporting skull likely to snap, initially bending nose out of shape

parts.note: someone cross is irritable and likely to snap

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word bending
out of shape means the letters of nose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a fragile skull and a broken, bent nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of shape' turns NOSE into ONES. The device is the pirate flag emblem, two bones crossed beneath a skull.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Jolly Roger, two crossed thigh-bones sit beneath the skull, holding it up.

parts.note: something remarkable is really something
rank means foul or rotten

explanation.surface: Something utterly remarkable, yet foul as well.
explanation.walkthrough: Used adverbially, as in spoiling a child something rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British idiom means to an extreme degree, utterly.

clue.text: One state has turned into another

indicators.note: into means the second piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan, one US state
milk that has turned is sour, so has turned gives is sour

explanation.surface: One US state transforming into a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has turned' is read as IS SOUR, which goes inside MI (Michigan).
explanation.definitionFit: The definition stands for another US state, the one called the Show-Me State.

clue.text: Chanting starts in third over during part of game

indicators.note: during means the starting letters fall within the other piece

parts.note: an inning is a division of a baseball game

indicators.note: starts in means take the opening letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cricket or baseball scene: something happening in the third over.
explanation.definitionFit: Intoning is reciting in a steady chanting voice.

indicators.note: admits means the girl lets the other word inside her

parts.note: a lass is a girl
trite means hackneyed and predictable

explanation.surface: A girl admits a last ceremony was dull and predictable.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the sacraments given to a dying person, the ultimate ceremony.

indicators.note: worried means troubled or agitated, so these letters are stirred about

explanation.surface: A political report: Liberals anxious about their opponents' notable gains.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means striking or outstanding, as in a signal victory.

indicators.note: left means the letter for one has departed from the phrase

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I; one's here means one has, as in one has left
poor means inadequate

explanation.surface: Someone complains their path is not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'one's left' as 'one has left': take I from IS POOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoor is the track or scent left by an animal.

clue.text: Area in pandemonium after soldiers lay down

indicators.note: after means the pandemonium piece follows the soldiers

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: in means the area letter goes inside the noise

parts.note: a din is uproar or pandemonium

explanation.surface: Troops in chaos are told to lay down their arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to decree or lay down as a rule.

clue.text: Prisoner hides hammer in piece of bread

indicators.note: hides means the prisoner conceals the other word inside

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
to hammer an opponent is to rout them

explanation.surface: A convict smuggling a hammer in a loaf, the classic file-in-a-cake escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammer' looks like a tool; it means to defeat heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cube of fried or toasted bread served in soup or salad.

parts.note: a tot is a small shot of spirits

explanation.surface: An elderly dog has been shot.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz.

parts.note: work is read as a verb, to function, which is to go, as in the engine goes
odd means irregular or unusual
ay is an old word for always

explanation.surface: An unpredictable job is always welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a greeting, a way of welcoming someone.

parts.note: yet means still, as in yet to come
I is the Roman numeral one, single

explanation.surface: An unattached person is told it is wonderful to remain single.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a creature of legend, imaginary.

clue.text: Land of Hope is song about burying beheaded fanatic

indicators.note: burying means the song's letters enclose the other piece
about means the word for a song is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a song

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a puritan is a zealot, a strict fanatic

explanation.surface: Land of Hope and Glory is a song, here wrapped around a headless zealot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AIR into RIA; 'beheaded' strips PURITAN to URITAN. Anthony Hope invented this land in The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: This fictional Central European kingdom is the setting of Anthony Hope's novels.

clue.text: Fiat 500 is car primarily wrapped in film

indicators.note: wrapped in means the earlier pieces are enclosed by the film

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an extraterrestrial
D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letters of the words is and car

explanation.surface: A Fiat 500 car appearing in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiat 500' reads as the Italian car; Fiat alone is the definition, and 500 is D.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative order or decree.
